descripcion: Persuasion in English leans on framing rather than force: presenting your proposal in terms of the other side's interest, offering conditional concessions, making it easy to say yes. The move that matters most is separating positions from interests — a position has one solution, an interest has several.

converts a position into a problem

*What would it take for this to work for you?*
*I can't do the full amount, but I can do it in two payments this month.*
*Suppose we tried it for three months and reviewed it.*
*I think we want the same thing here; we just disagree about how.*

notas: Conditional offers concede nothing until reciprocated. That is why they are the workhorse.
*What would it take?* is the most useful negotiating question in English.
Giving a reason materially increases compliance, even a weak one. *Because* does real work.

contraste.es: Spanish has the same conditional language for opening positions (nuestra propuesta inicial sería… – our starting point would be…), so the phrases transfer. What needs practice is setting an ambitious first figure and justifying it, since English treats the first offer as an anchor.
contraste.de: Unser Ausgangspunkt wäre… corresponds exactly to our starting point would be…, with the same conditional. The language of anchoring therefore transfers directly.
contraste.it: La nostra proposta iniziale sarebbe… corresponds exactly to our starting point would be…, with the same conditional. The language of anchoring therefore transfers directly.
contraste.fr: Notre proposition de départ serait… corresponds exactly to our starting point would be…, with the same conditional. The language of anchoring therefore transfers directly.
contraste.pt: A nossa proposta inicial seria… corresponds exactly to our starting point would be…, with the same conditional. The language of anchoring therefore transfers directly.

errores: *I want* repeated — replace with *I'm looking for*, *what would help is*, *my constraint is*.
Conceding without a counter-ask, which resets expectations for the whole negotiation.
Confusing persuasion with volume or repetition.

mision.consigna: Negotiate something real about your housing — a rent increase, a repair, a deposit deduction.
requisitos: one explicit reframe from position to interest
one concession that asks for something back

microtareas.texto: Write your position on something in one line, then the interest underneath it.
Write three conditional offers that give nothing unless the other side moves.
Record 90 seconds making a case for a repair, starting from the landlord's interest, not yours.

autochequeo: Did I frame in terms of their interest or mine?
Did I anchor, or open at my minimum?
Did I give a reason for each ask?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on persuasion and negotiation. (1) Check each conditional offer for unilateral concession. (2) Say whose interest I framed around. (3) Flag any concession without a counter-ask. (4) Rewrite my opening so it anchors higher without sounding unreasonable. Do not rewrite the rest.
